Issued at 300 AM EDT Fri Aug 21 2026

Today-Tonight...The mid-level low begins to weaken across 
northern Florida today as troughing across the eastern US extends 
southward towards it. At the surface, this will result in the 
Atlantic high remaining well south of the area, with a quasi- 
stationary boundary draped across the southeastern US slowly 
drifting a bit southward. A plume of moisture will maintain itself
across Florida, with PWATs forecast to exceed 2" areawide. Light 
southwest winds continue at the surface, with a bit more of a 
southerly component aloft through this morning assisting with an 
easier development and push inland of the east coast sea breeze 
this afternoon. Scattered showers and storms are forecast, with 
PoPs remaining between 30-50%. Some Saharan dust drifting across 
the peninsula will maintain a pocket of drier air between 850-500 
mb today along with cooler temperatures aloft (around -8C). This 
combined with adequate daytime heating supporting plenty of 
instability will favor scattered storm development, with storm 
hazards include frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts up to 55 
mph, small hail, and heavy downpours resulting in 1-3" of rainfall
across the area. Marginally severe wind gusts cannot be ruled out
given the drier air aloft. Additionally, light steering flow will
increase the potential for erratic and slow storm motions, which 
will mean there is a greater risk of minor, localized flooding in 
some spots. Activity will generally push offshore across the local
Atlantic waters, with mostly dry conditions through the overnight
hours.

Heat persists across east central Florida, with highs in the low 
to mid 90s. Peak heat indices are forecast to reach 102F to 107F, 
remaining just below Heat Advisory criteria. However, the risk of 
developing heat-related illness remains high across the area, so 
residents and visitors alike are strongly encouraged to practice 
heat safety today. Remain well-hydrated, take breaks in the shade 
or an air conditioned building, and wear lightweight, lightly 
colored clothing. Never leave children or pets unattended in 
vehicles. Near normal temperatures overnight with lows in the mid 
70s.

Saturday-Sunday...Mid-level troughing across the eastern US will 
extend southward through this weekend, absorbing the mid-level 
low. The surface Atlantic high will continue to remain south of 
east central Florida, and the quasi-stationary boundary will 
continue southward as the upper level support pushes it south. The
typical diurnal pattern will persist, with afternoon showers and 
storms being driven by the development and interaction of the sea 
breezes. PoPs remain in the 30-50% range each afternoon, with the 
usual storm hazards all in play; lightning strikes, gusty winds, 
and heavy downpours. Dry air aloft from the Saharan dust will 
continue to increase the risk of strong to marginally severe wind 
gusts, though most wind gusts should remain at or below 55 mph. 
Additionally, minor, localized flooding will continue to be a 
potential concern due to light steering flow aloft and cooler 
temperatures around 500 mb will maintain the risk of small hail 
development. Light offshore steering flow will result in activity 
pushing off the coast and out across the local Atlantic waters 
each evening, with mostly dry conditions through the overnight 
hours across east central Florida.

Temperatures are forecast to remain near-normal through this 
weekend, with highs in the low 90s and lows in the mid 70s. While 
guidance continues to favor remaining below advisory criteria, 
peak heat indices are still anticipated to reach the 102F-107F 
range. If spending extended periods of time outdoors this weekend,
be sure to practice heat safety to avoid developing heat-related 
illness. 

Monday-Thursday...The mid-level troughing across the eastern US 
lifts northeastward into next week, resulting in a lift northward 
of the stalled boundary across the southeastern US. This will 
allow the Atlantic high to lift northward, with the ridge axis 
forecast to establish itself across central Florida once again. 
While the pattern itself will change very minimally from the 
typical afternoon showers and storms, there will be a change in 
wind direction from a predominantly offshore component to more of 
a southerly component. This has implications on how far inland the
east coast sea breeze will be able to push as well as where the 
highest rain and storm chances will be focused (more across the 
interior rather than the east coast). It is worth noting that 
guidance has trended drier on Monday due to some Saharan air 
potentially drifting towards the peninsula resulting in PoPs 
falling to 20-30%, but there remains some uncertainty with this 
still. Overall, the typical summertime pattern is forecast to 
persist, with lightning, gusty winds, and heavy downpours all 
possible with activity. Temperatures are anticipated to remain 
near-normal through next week
